slides.title: CSC SCHOLARSHIP 2027
slides.sub: The complete application process, step by step

items.say: Every year, the Chinese government gives thousands of international students a fully funded degree in China. Free tuition, a free dorm, medical insurance, and a monthly stipend.
In this video, I'll walk you through the entire application process for the C S C scholarship, from choosing a university, to getting your visa. Step by step, with nothing skipped.
Save this video, because you'll want to come back to it while you apply. Let's get started.
Chapter one. What does the Chinese Government Scholarship actually give you?
First, your tuition fees are completely covered.
Second, you get a free university dormitory, or an accommodation subsidy if you live off campus.
Third, comprehensive medical insurance for international students.

And fourth, a monthly stipend. The standard rates are two thousand five hundred yuan a month for bachelor's students, three thousand for master's students, and three thousand five hundred for P H D students.
The one thing that's not covered is your flight to China. Plan for that.
Chapter two. There are two main ways to apply, and choosing the right one matters.
Type A is the bilateral program. You apply through the dispatching authority in your home country, which is usually the Chinese embassy, or your country's education ministry.
Type A applications usually open around January and close by early April, but your embassy sets the exact deadline, so always check their notice.
Type B is the Chinese University Program. You apply directly to one Chinese university, which then nominates you for the scholarship.
Each university sets its own Type B deadline. Many fall between December and March, so start early.
Important: you can only submit one Type B application per year. So choose your university carefully.
items.b: Only *ONE* Type B application per year

items.say: Chapter three. Are you eligible?
You must be a non Chinese citizen, in good physical and mental health.
For a bachelor's degree, you need a high school diploma, and you must be under twenty five.
For a master's degree, you need a bachelor's degree, and you must be under thirty five.
For a P H D, you need a master's degree, and you must be under forty.
For English taught programs, most universities ask for IELTS or TOEFL, or proof that your last degree was taught in English. For Chinese taught programs, you'll need an H S K certificate.
Bachelor's applicants should also know that a new test, the C S C A, is now required, so register for it before your deadline.
Now let's go through the process itself. Step one: choose your university and program.
Go to campus china dot org, and check which universities accept Chinese Government Scholarship students in your field.
Then open the university's own international admissions website, and read their scholarship notice for this year.
Write down the university's agency number. Every university has one. For example, Wuhan University's is one zero four eight six, and Sichuan University's is one zero six one zero.
This number is critical. If you enter the wrong agency number, your application will not reach the university.
Step two. Try to get a pre admission or acceptance letter from a professor.
For master's and P H D programs, a professor's acceptance letter is often optional, but applicants who have one get priority. It can make a big difference.
Find professors in your field on the university's department pages, and read a couple of their recent papers.
Then send a short, polite email. Introduce yourself, explain why their research matches your interests, and attach your C V and research proposal.
Email several professors, not just one, and follow up politely after a week or two if you don't hear back.
Step three. Prepare your documents. This takes the longest, so start early.
Your passport information page. Make sure your passport stays valid well beyond the date the university asks for.
Your highest degree certificate and your transcripts, notarized. If they're not in Chinese or English, you'll need certified translations.
A study plan or research proposal. Master's and P H D applicants usually need at least eight hundred words, and some universities ask for more.
Two recommendation letters from professors or associate professors, for master's and P H D applicants.
Your language certificate, like IELTS, TOEFL, or H S K, depending on your program.
The Foreigner Physical Examination Form, completed by a doctor, with your blood test results. It's usually valid for six months.
A non criminal record certificate, usually issued within six months before you apply.
And if you have one, your professor's acceptance letter.
Scan everything clearly, in color. Unclear scans can get your application rejected.

slides.title: Step 4: Apply on the CSC portal

items.say: Step four. Submit your application on the official C S C portal.
Go to study in china dot C S C dot edu dot c n, create an account, and log in.
Fill in your personal information first. You can't start the application until this part is complete.
Next, choose your program category, Type A or Type B, and enter the agency number of your embassy or university.
Fill in your study details, language ability and study plan, then upload all your documents.
Check everything carefully before you press submit. After submitting, you can't edit it, unless you withdraw it before it's accepted.
Finally, download and print your application form, sign it, and upload the signed copy wherever your university asks for it.
Step five. For Type B, and for many Type A universities too, you also apply on the university's own portal.
Register on the university's international student application system.
Choose Chinese Government Scholarship as your funding type, select your program, and upload the same documents.
Submit before the university's deadline. You need both applications, C S C and university. Missing either one usually means you won't be considered.
Chapter nine. What happens after you apply?
First, the university or embassy reviews your application. Some universities hold online interviews, so check your email often.
Shortlisted candidates are recommended to the China Scholarship Council for final approval.
Final results usually come out around July or August. You can check your status in the C S C system.
Winners receive an admission letter, and a visa form called J W two oh one or J W two oh two.
Take these to the Chinese embassy to apply for your X one student visa, and get ready to fly to China in late August or September.
Chapter ten. The mistakes that get applications rejected.
Number one: entering the wrong agency number.
Number two: submitting only the C S C application, and forgetting the university application, or the other way around.
Number three: a generic study plan. Make it specific to the program and the professor.
Number four: blurry scans, or expired documents.
And number five: paying an agent. The China Scholarship Council does not use any agents. Applying is free, and you can do it all yourself.

slides.title: YOU CAN DO THIS
slides.sub: New scholarships every day on Scholarships in China

items.say: That's the complete process. Choose your university, contact professors, prepare your documents, and submit both applications before the deadline.
Every day on this channel, we share a new fully funded scholarship with its deadline and agency number. Subscribe, so you don't miss the one that's right for you.
And if you have a question, drop it in the comments. Good luck with your application!
